subject: PSHE
title: Safe choices and asking for help
outcome: Practise help-seeking and decision-making in scenarios.
lesson_outcomes: Practise help-seeking and decision-making in scenarios.
theme_status: Original lesson grouping, not a verbatim scheme theme.
credit: Lesson resource · CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for classroom use, share and adapt with credit, no resale
definition: A decision is a choice about what to do. A safe choice respects people and avoids adding harm. Help-seeking means asking a trusted adult for support. A person can ask when unsure and does not need proof first.
routine: Think about a safe choice and why it fits. A trusted adult can help make the choice.
Choose a safe step, phrase or request. A pause or asking an adult is an action too. No one must confront a person or solve harm alone.
Ask a trusted adult or school staff in private when help is needed. Say what the concern is and ask what will happen next. If help is not enough, ask another trusted adult.
routine_rule: Decide, act and tell are prompts, not a fixed order. If unsafe or unsure, tell a trusted adult first. There is no need to try a phrase, resolve a problem or collect proof before help. Staff use the safeguarding lead through school procedure.
help: Ask a trusted adult or school staff privately. Say Can we talk in private? I need help with a choice or concern. Use words, a note, HELP or a usual aid. If the first adult is busy or help is not enough, ask another trusted adult. For an urgent safety concern, get adult help at once through the school route.
step_out: Before teaching, agree a discreet HELP or PAUSE signal, available adult and familiar supervised place and route. Staff acknowledge it quietly and keep adult support. No public reason is needed. Offer a neutral task, supported return or private catch-up. No learner leaves alone.
safeguarding: Any disclosure goes to the safeguarding lead through school procedure. Listen calmly, reassure, do not probe, investigate or promise secrecy. Follow urgent school procedures for immediate concerns. Keep real concerns and identifying details in the separate safeguarding record, not learning evidence. A pupil unable to identify a trusted adult is supported privately, not pressed.
privacy: All tasks use invented third-person scenes. No real relationship, health, family, account, password or incident is requested. Pass and the agreed pause are valid. Any optional personal card stays with the pupil and is not collected, photographed, displayed or compared. Only fictional learning is kept as evidence.

cases.title: A turn with a shared card shape
cases.text: Two invented learners want the same card shape for a small display. Both need a short turn. One learner wants help to agree whose turn comes next.
cases.decide: A fair turn plan can let both use the shape.
cases.act: I would like us to agree a turn. They could listen and use a swap cue, or ask staff to help.
cases.tell: Ask trusted school staff for help if they cannot agree or feel unsure. Can we talk in private? We need help with a fair turn plan.
cases.reason: A clear plan respects both views. The learner need not give in or argue to be heard.

cases.title: A request to share a photo
cases.text: In an invented group chat, a learner is asked to pass on a photo of another learner's work. They do not know if that learner agreed. No real photo, message or account is shown.
cases.decide: Pause before sharing. Check permission and private details with trusted adult help.
cases.act: No. I will ask first. They can stop replying and ask a trusted adult before any share. They do not copy or forward private or harmful content as proof.
cases.tell: Tell a trusted adult or school staff privately if unsure or pressured. Ask for help with a safe report or block route if needed.
cases.reason: A group request does not make sharing right. Private settings cannot stop every copy.

cases.title: A fair way to join the group task
cases.text: An invented group plans a small display. One learner wants everyone to write. Another would like to draw or use their usual aid. The group has not yet heard each idea.
cases.decide: Choose a fair way for each learner to be heard and use usual access.
cases.act: Can we hear each idea? I would like a fair way for each person to take part. The group can ask staff to help plan options.
cases.tell: Ask a trusted adult or school staff if someone is left out or the plan still does not feel fair. Can you help us find a way for each person to take part?
cases.reason: Respect includes listening and helping people take part. A shared rule does not make unfair treatment right.

choices.task: Decide act tell map or list

same_evidence: Choose a response format, not one scene. Both formats cover all three scenes: a safe choice with a reason, a safe action or phrase, and a trusted-adult help route. When unsafe or unsure, telling first is always valid.

routes.Supported: Use both the routine and model. Work through each scene in short parts. Choose between two safe lines if needed. Point, type, use a usual aid or exact scribe/readback. Keep normal access apart from content cues.
routes.Independent: Use usual aids and the visible model. For all three scenes, explain a safe choice, action or phrase, and private help route. Explain when telling first is best.
routes.Aspire: For each scene compare two safe options. Explain a reason and a fallback if the first plan or adult route does not help. Do not collect proof, confront harm or add personal detail.

success: For all three invented scenes, choose a safe next step with a reason.
Give a safe action or phrase and a private trusted-adult help route.
Explain that help can come first, and improve one response after feedback.

scaffolds.model: Ask staff to help plan fair turns.
They could pause before sharing because permission is not clear.
I would like us to agree a turn.
Add which trusted adult role could help.
Ask another trusted adult through the agreed route.

hinge.question: A learner is unsure whether a group request is safe. What fits the routine?
choices: A They must act before asking anyone.
B They can tell a trusted adult first.
C They need to collect proof first.
D They should keep the concern secret.
hinge.parallel: The first adult is busy. A Ask another trusted adult through the agreed route. B Stop asking and deal with the concern alone.
hinge.rule: Check privately. B or safe equivalent with a reason: proceed. A makes the prompts a rigid order; C wrongly requires proof; D accepts secrecy. Re-model and use parallel A. A pass or no response is not observed, never a failure label.

timing: Settle; agree help and supervised pause. Recall a safe choice or explain its reason.
Read both exact outcomes. Explain decide, act and tell, with tell-first safety rule.
Model one small part of each scene. Match a step or improve unsafe advice.
Check tell-first/help without proof. Choose a response format and usual mode.
A22–26, B26–30, C30–34; map/list or three short notes. All three offered.
Check all responses; one NS and actual own reply. Staff note current/prior evidence.
Explain a help route or repair a myth. Close with support.
assessment: This is the assessing week. The six-outcome tick-and-comment grid starts blank and spans rows 70 to 75 across five teaching weeks. Use Week 5a and Week 5b for the two final outcomes. Record actual current or prior work references, context, usual access and content prompts. Tick observed, more learning needed or not observed honestly, and explain gaps or the next chance. A pass is not observed. One fictional task cannot prove every outcome or lasting behaviour. The grid is not criteria for the unit award. Staff check actual requirements and evidence sufficiency before offering evidence. No automatic banking or award follows from completion.

paragraphs: Practise help-seeking and decision-making in scenarios.
All people and scenes are made up. Use only the stories. No real concern, account or private detail is needed. Keep your usual aids. Pass or ask for the agreed pause if you need.
In your book, make a decide, act and tell map or list for each of A, B and C. Give a reason. Help can come first.
In your book, write one short note for each of A, B and C. Use the same checks. Each note needs a choice and reason, safe action or phrase, and private adult-help route.
For all three made-up scenes, give a safe choice and a reason, a safe action or phrase, and a private trusted-adult help route. Tell first if unsafe or unsure. Improve one response after feedback.
Model: I would like us to agree a turn.
Model: Can we hear each idea?
Decide, act and tell are prompts, not a rule about order. If unsafe or unsure, tell a trusted adult first. You do not need proof or a first try before help.
Ready to explain [ ]    With a prompt [ ]    Need another example [ ]
All boxes start blank. Check learning about the stories, not real behaviour or wellbeing. Keep your first try, one next step and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode.
Choose a map/list or three notes. Complete all three made-up scenes. Use a work code, never a name, real concern or account detail. Ask for an exact scribe and quiet readback if useful.
Save using the usual routine, lesson code and work code. A book, line choices, usual aid or exact scribe is also valid. An adult reads back quietly so you can correct your words.
PSHE-GROW-S2-W05 E1 · Wednesday 24 March 2027 · P3 · assessing week

Staff: use a work code, not a name. All boxes start blank. Use current work or a valid prior record. Add what it shows, usual aids, content prompts and the next chance. Tick observed, more learning needed or not observed. Explain support and gaps in the comment. These are learning judgements, not criteria for the unit award.

paragraphs: Practise help-seeking and decision-making in scenarios.

A decision is a choice about what to do. A safe choice respects people and avoids adding harm. Help-seeking means asking a trusted adult for support. A person can ask when unsure and does not need proof first.
Think about a safe choice and why it fits. A trusted adult can help make the choice.
Choose a safe step, phrase or request. A pause or asking an adult is an action too. No one must confront a person or solve harm alone.
Ask a trusted adult or school staff in private when help is needed. Say what the concern is and ask what will happen next. If help is not enough, ask another trusted adult.

Decide, act and tell are prompts, not a fixed order. If unsafe or unsure, tell a trusted adult first. There is no need to try a phrase, resolve a problem or collect proof before help. Staff use the safeguarding lead through school procedure.

Choose a response format, not one scene. Both formats cover all three scenes: a safe choice with a reason, a safe action or phrase, and a trusted-adult help route. When unsafe or unsure, telling first is always valid. Both formats use the same checks and ordinary aids. A map needs no art skill. Notes need no extra length.

A A turn with a shared card shape

A fair turn plan can let both use the shape. I would like us to agree a turn. They could listen and use a swap cue, or ask staff to help. Ask trusted school staff for help if they cannot agree or feel unsure. Can we talk in private? We need help with a fair turn plan. Reason: A clear plan respects both views. The learner need not give in or argue to be heard. Accept other fitting safe choices, phrases and adult routes.
B A request to share a photo

Pause before sharing. Check permission and private details with trusted adult help. No. I will ask first. They can stop replying and ask a trusted adult before any share. They do not copy or forward private or harmful content as proof. Tell a trusted adult or school staff privately if unsure or pressured. Ask for help with a safe report or block route if needed. Reason: A group request does not make sharing right. Private settings cannot stop every copy. Accept other fitting safe choices, phrases and adult routes.
C A fair way to join the group task

Choose a fair way for each learner to be heard and use usual access. Can we hear each idea? I would like a fair way for each person to take part. The group can ask staff to help plan options. Ask a trusted adult or school staff if someone is left out or the plan still does not feel fair. Can you help us find a way for each person to take part? Reason: Respect includes listening and helping people take part. A shared rule does not make unfair treatment right. Accept other fitting safe choices, phrases and adult routes.

Main B. A makes the prompts a fixed order. C wrongly requires proof. D accepts secrecy. Re-model then use parallel A: ask another trusted adult through the agreed route. A pass is unobserved; check privately in the usual mode.

Help can come before deciding or acting. The pupil need not confront a person, try a phrase or gather proof. A group request does not grant permission to share. Fair participation includes usual aids and hearing each learner. No one must solve harm alone.
